expectations.text: Decides on the commoditization test rather than on whether the 18-month engineer commitment is affordable
expectations.evidence: The answer leads with "The commoditization test kills all three before staffing or venue even come up," and labels that test "decisive," tying it to the user's own words ("the entire product is the scoring model and the score API around it") to show the proposed standard covers the product itself, not an adjacent seam. It explicitly caps posture at Extend on that basis ("naming your own product as the layer sets the ceiling at Extend. Contribute, Co-found, and Drive are off the table"), and even discounts the demand test as not deciding anything "because the next test already caps the posture

expectations.text: Decides on the commoditization test rather than on whether the 18-month engineer commitment is affordable
expectations.evidence: The verdict is justified immediately and explicitly by the commoditize-your-complement logic, not by cost: 'you're one scoring vendor being asked to chair a standard written by six platform vendors... Platforms have a standing, well-documented incentive to commoditize their complements — the more interchangeable the scoring layer becomes, the more value accrues to the platform... You're being asked to spend 18 months of your only senior engineer designing the mechanism that makes you replaceable.' The engineer's time is framed as what gets spent building one's own replacement, not as a budget
